content.value_statement: Teams lose time when code behavior and setup steps are unclear. This skill drafts docstrings, README sections, API references, and comments using practical templates.
actual_capabilities: Generates language-specific docstring templates for JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Go, and Rust.
Drafts README sections for installation, quick start, usage, API reference, configuration, contributing, and license.
Creates documentation checklists for functions, classes, modules, and files.
Documents options objects, callbacks, generic types, parameters, return values, errors, and examples.
Supports coordination with related documentation skills named in the skill instructions.
limitations: Does not verify that example commands or package names exist.
Does not run tests or execute examples because allowed tools are documentation file tools.
Requires accurate code context from the user or repository to avoid stale descriptions.
May need human review for product tone, legal notices, and project-specific conventions.

use_cases.title: Document Public APIs
use_cases.description: Create consistent API references with parameters, return values, errors, and examples.

use_cases.title: Add Code Docstrings
use_cases.description: Write language-specific docstrings for functions, classes, modules, callbacks, and generic types.

use_cases.title: Refresh Project Guides
use_cases.description: Update README content for setup, quick start, usage, configuration, contribution, and license sections.

prompt_templates.title: Document a Function
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one code unit.
prompt_templates.prompt: Document the selected function. Include its purpose, parameters, return value, errors, and one short example.

prompt_templates.title: Create a README
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a README for this project. Include overview, features, prerequisites, installation, quick start, usage, configuration, and license sections.

prompt_templates.title: Write API Reference
prompt_templates.prompt: Write API documentation for the provided module. Group related functions and document inputs, outputs, errors, side effects, and examples.

prompt_templates.title: Rebuild Documentation Set
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced documentation refresh across a repository.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the repository documentation and propose a complete update plan. Then draft the highest priority docs with style and terminology consistency.

output_examples.input: A public function lacks parameter and error documentation.
output: A concise summary line explains the function purpose.
Each parameter is described with type, meaning, defaults, and constraints.
Return values, possible errors, and a short usage example are included.

output_examples.input: A project needs a README before release.
output: The README starts with project purpose and key features.
Setup steps cover prerequisites, installation, and first run.
Usage, configuration, contribution, and license sections are organized for scanning.

output_examples.input: A module exposes callbacks and generic result types.
output: Callback signatures are named and explained in plain language.
Generic type parameters describe success and error values.
Examples show expected behavior without hiding edge cases.

best_practices: Provide the relevant code, current docs, and audience before asking for generated documentation.
Review examples against real behavior before publishing them.
Keep generated documentation aligned with the repository style and naming conventions.
anti_patterns: Do not publish placeholder commands, URLs, or package names without replacement.
Do not use generated docs as a substitute for testing examples.
Do not ask for broad documentation rewrites without source context and priorities.

faq.question: What types of documentation can this skill write?
faq.answer: It can write docstrings, README sections, API references, code comments, module notes, and documentation checklists.

faq.question: Which programming languages are covered?
faq.answer: The included templates cover JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Go, and Rust documentation patterns.

faq.question: Does the skill execute code examples?
faq.answer: No. It writes documentation and examples, but it does not run commands or verify execution results.

faq.question: Can it update an existing README?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the current README and project context so it can revise sections consistently.

faq.question: Is it useful with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: What should users review before publishing?
faq.answer: Users should check technical accuracy, placeholder values, working examples, product tone, legal notices, and project conventions.
